issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for an execution application seeking correction and restitution of land wrongly recorded as delivered symbolically begins when an actual threat of dispossession arises.
material_facts: In execution of a decree, symbolic possession was wrongly recorded over land beyond the decree-holder’s entitlement, while the judgment-debtor’s predecessor remained in possession.
A declaratory decree challenging the symbolic-possession entry became final.
The decree-holder later filed partition proceedings claiming the land, creating an actual threat of dispossession, and the judgment-debtors then applied for correction and restitution.
issues.conclusion: The right to apply accrued when the actual threat of dispossession began with the partition proceedings, not when symbolic possession was recorded; the High Court was wrong to treat the application as time-barred from the earlier date.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the three-year period runs from when the right to apply accrues, which depends on the facts and circumstances of the case. Where an application seeks recovery of possession following dispossession, the Court relied on Merla Ramanna v. Nallaparaju and Others, applying Article 181 (corresponding to Article 137), for the principle that the application is in time if made within three years of dispossession.

rule.if: execution_restitution_application and erroneous_symbolic_entry and applicant_remained_in_possession and actual_threat_of_dispossession

predicates.execution_restitution_application: A party applied in execution proceedings to correct a delivery record and obtain restitution of land.
predicates.erroneous_symbolic_entry: The execution record wrongly stated that symbolic possession had been delivered over land beyond the decree-holder’s entitlement.
predicates.applicant_remained_in_possession: The applicant or the applicant’s predecessor continued to possess the land despite the symbolic-possession entry.
predicates.actual_threat_of_dispossession: The decree-holder took proceedings asserting a claim to the land that threatened to remove the applicant from possession.

issues.definition: When a party seeks restitution of land wrongly recorded as symbolically delivered, remained in possession, and faces an actual threat of dispossession, the limitation period begins when that threat arises.

issues.legal_issue: An executing court may correct a mistaken record of symbolic possession over land exceeding the decree and order restitution of that land.
material_facts: The execution record mistakenly included symbolic delivery of land beyond the decree-holder’s entitlement.
The judgment-debtor’s predecessor remained in possession, and a declaratory decree challenging the symbolic-possession entry became final and binding on the decree-holder.
The judgment-debtors applied in the executing court for correction and restitution; that court granted relief, but the High Court set its order aside.
issues.conclusion: The executing court rightly corrected the error and ordered restitution; the Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s judgment and restored the executing court’s judgment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld correction on an objection under Sections 47 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It also relied on the final and binding declaratory decree concerning the erroneous entry.

predicates.execution_correction_application: A party asked the executing court to correct the execution record and restore land.
predicates.symbolic_delivery_exceeded_decree: The executing court’s record mistakenly extended symbolic delivery to land not covered by the decree-holder’s entitlement.
predicates.final_declaratory_decree: A declaratory judgment holding the symbolic-possession entry improper became final and binding on the decree-holder.

issues.definition: When an execution correction application concerns symbolic delivery mistakenly extending beyond the decree and a final declaratory decree confirms the error, the executing court may correct the record and order restitution.
